en.title: Wolverine's 'Fart Gas' Trail: Insomniac Clarifies In-Game Navigation
en.summary: A peculiar debate has erupted over the visual cues in Marvel's Wolverine, with players questioning the persistent 'fart gas' scent trail. Developer Insomniac Games has stepped in to clarify its purpose and availability.
en.body:
The upcoming **Marvel's Wolverine** has already sparked a unique conversation among fans, centering on a visual element described by some as “fart gas.” This refers to the scent trail Wolverine leaves behind as he tracks targets, a feature revealed earlier this summer. Recently, the debate resurfaced online, particularly after a journalist from The Washington Post pointed out that the trail persists even when other navigation aids are turned off, leading to calls for Insomniac Games to provide an option to disable it entirely.

Confusion arose as players experimented with the game's accessibility options. While **Marvel's Wolverine** does include features like 'Chase Assist' to aid in pursuit sequences, this does not affect the scent trail. Similarly, other navigation toggles, such as mission waypoints, can be disabled, but the distinctive green trail remains visible. This led to the assumption that the scent trail is a permanent fixture, prompting community requests for its removal or an off-switch.

## The Developer's Clarification

Insomniac Games, through its director of community and marketing, **James Stevenson**, has now addressed the growing discussion. Stevenson clarified on social media that the scent trail is *not* always active in the game. He emphasized its narrative and gameplay significance, stating, “It represents Logan’s canon mutant super senses and elite tracking ability.” According to Insomniac, the trail only appears when Wolverine is actively tracking a specific scent or sound, such as a person, a spilled drink like whisky, or other clues crucial to story or mission progression. It also shows up when players are hunting for collectibles. This means the visual cue is intentionally tied to specific gameplay moments rather than being a constant overlay.

## Fan Reactions and the 'Fart Gas' Phenomenon

The term 'fart gas' itself highlights the sometimes humorous, sometimes critical lens through which players view game mechanics. While some players appreciate the visual representation of Wolverine's unique powers and the added layer of immersion it provides, others find it distracting or unnecessary. The inability to toggle it off, coupled with its distinct visual style, has unfortunately led to its less-than-flattering nickname. The discussion showcases the ongoing challenge for developers to balance faithful representation of iconic characters with the diverse preferences and accessibility needs of their player base. Many fans are eager to see how **Wolverine**'s signature tracking abilities translate into gameplay, and this visual element is a key part of that experience, even if it has generated some lighthearted controversy.

## What's Next

As **Marvel's Wolverine** nears its release, Insomniac Games continues to refine the player experience based on feedback. While the scent trail's functionality has been explained, further details on accessibility or potential adjustments will likely emerge closer to launch. Fans can anticipate more gameplay reveals and developer insights in the coming months.

content_raw: A debate over “fart gas” has emerged around PlayStation 5 exclusive Marvel’s Wolverine , with some people calling for developer Insomniac to add the ability to disable Logan’s scent trail entirely from the game. Marvel’s Wolverine will show a scent trail for Logan to follow in certain circumstances, which had been revealed and already discussed earlier this summer . The debate around this was rekindled following the publication of Marvel’s Wolverine reviews online this week, with The Washington Post journalist Gene Park calling the scent trail “fart gas” because of the way it appears behind characters Logan follows. Jean Grey’s fart gas trail is NOT part of the navigation assist option. i turned it on and there’s another green line that tells you where to go. mission waypoint (yellow marker) is on as well and THAT can be turned off. 2nd pic i turn off the options and the gas stays. it seems… pic.twitter.com/cKs9uTPSG0 — Gene Park (@GenePark) September 10, 2026 There was some confusion online about the ability to turn this feature off via accessibility options. Insomniac’s official list of accessibility options for Wolverine includes a “Chase Assist,” which lets you toggle reduced movement speed for targets during chase sequences, but it does not turn off the trail. Other navigation toggles do not turn off the scent trail either. This has in turn led some to believe the scent trail is always on in-game, and so have called on Insomniac to add in the ability to turn it off. But Insomniac’s director of community and marketing, James Stevenson, took to social media to nip that suggestion in the bud. “The scent trail isn’t always on,” he clarified. “It represents Logan’s canon mutant super senses and elite tracking ability. It only is there when he’s tracking a specific scent / sound (a person, whisky, or another clue scent) - story/mission moments or when he catches whiff of a collectible.” Despite this, some still want to get rid of the “fart gas” entirely. The criticism here is that the scent trail holds the player’s hand too strongly. Referencing previous discourse about Final Fantasy’s yellow paint guides , some have said these lines remove any potential skill required for a chase sequence, for example, or exploration. This in turn has sparked questions about the difficulty of adapting Wolverine for a video game. Given his canon mutant powers, Logan probably wouldn’t spend much time wandering through levels looking for his target — or his next drink — but that doesn’t make for particularly exciting gameplay. Some have suggested that Logan’s scent power could be something the player can trigger with a press of R3 on the DualSense, so there’s a way for players to avoid using it if they feel that strongly about it. Based on Stevenson’s post, Insomniac didn’t feel that would make sense for Logan.
